claims.text: Overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms.
A stable oxide layer forms on the coating at high operating temperatures.
The stable oxide layer enhances wear resistance by reducing adhesive wear.
The stable oxide layer mitigates microscopic deformation by promoting more uniform deformation.
The baseline coating is 20 μm thick and is deposited by magnetron sputtering at 500°C.
The controlled intervention raises the coating deposition temperature from 500°C to 700°C while holding all other deposition parameters constant.
Raising the deposition temperature to 700°C promotes formation or growth of a stable surface oxide layer.
The stable surface oxide layer is Cr2O3-rich.
Dislocation glide contributes to deformation in the stated high-temperature sliding regime.
Grain-boundary sliding contributes to deformation in the stated high-temperature sliding regime.
Formation of the oxide layer influences dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding.
The intervention reduces wear rate by 25%, from 1.0e-4 to 7.5e-5 mm^3/(N·m).
The intervention reduces average surface roughness by 30%, from 0.5 μm to 0.35 μm.
A reduction in average surface roughness represents a reduction in microscopic deformation.
The predictions are intended to hold at operating temperatures from 500°C to 800°C and a sliding velocity of 1 m/s.
Failure to achieve at least a 15% wear-resistance improvement and a 20% microscopic-deformation improvement after increasing deposition temperature from 500°C to 700°C falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says microscopic deformation should decrease, whereas the falsification rule literally requires microscopic deformation to increase by at least 20%. If the intended variable is resistance to deformation or a reduction in deformation, the rule must be rephrased accordingly.
